Search results support ITLN2 as a Paneth cell marker in the human small intestine, with the strongest evidence coming from a 2022 FASEB study and a 2022 single-cell atlas.

- **Bulk-level specificity:** A FASEB study by Nonnecke and colleagues reports that ITLN2 is among the most abundant products of Paneth cells, where it sits in secretory granules and forms multimers in the small intestine. ITLN2 is a highly abundant Paneth cell-specific product, which localizes to secretory granules, and is expressed as a multimeric protein in the small intestine.
- **Disease context:** The same study found ITLN2 mRNA roughly five-fold lower in ileal Crohn's disease specimens, and it was absent from healthy colon but expressed by metaplastic Paneth cells in colitis. ITLN2 mRNA expression was undetectable in control colon tissue; however, in both ulcerative colitis (UC) and colonic CD, metaplastic Paneth cells were found to express ITLN2.
- **Single-cell evidence:** Burclaff, Bliton and colleagues' single-cell atlas of healthy adult human small intestine and colon (12,590 epithelial cells from 3 donors) identifies a small-intestine cluster that expresses Paneth markers including ITLN2. An ITLN1-high cluster, all from SI, contains cells expressing PC markers (DEFA5, DEFA6, ITLN2, LYZ) along with cells expressing the GC marker MUC2. The same atlas warns that some common markers are not exclusive: Lysozyme expression is not unique to human Paneth cells, so ITLN2 may be a more specific choice than lysozyme.
- **Human Protein Atlas:** The Human Protein Atlas classifies ITLN2 as cell-type enriched in Paneth cells at the single-cell level, and as tissue enriched in intestine. Cell type enriched (Paneth cells)

Caveat: the atlas and the FASEB paper are the primary sources here; I did not retrieve full single-cell expression values for ITLN2 itself, so the magnitude of specificity should be checked directly in the Human Protein Atlas single-cell tab or the atlas data.

I saved the refined list as **small_intestine_147328_refined**. It passes `check_marker_list` with no errors or warnings, every gene is in the 480-gene panel, and it now has 47 types (your list had 36). Load it in Markers… → load a list…, then click Annotate.

Your list turned out to be the same as the built-in `small_intestine` list, so comparing the two added nothing. All your names, types and structure are kept. Here is what I changed:

**Markers that didn't tell siblings apart**
- **BEST4+ enterocytes and M cells:** both use SPIB, so I added negatives to each: M cells are BEST4−/OTOP2−, and BEST4+ enterocytes are CCL20−. Enterocytes are now BEST4−/OTOP2−.
- **Dendritic cells:** a cell had to express CLEC9A, CLEC10A, LAMP3 and CCR7 together, but these mark three different DC subsets. The type now needs any one of CLEC9A, CLEC10A or LAMP3 (and C1QB−), and it has three children: **cDC1** (CLEC9A, IRF8), **cDC2** (CLEC10A) and **Migratory DCs** (LAMP3, CCR7, FSCN1, IL4I1).
- **Blood vessel EC:** ACKR1 is a vein-only marker, so arterial cells were missed. It is now PECAM1 plus VWF or PLVAP (LYVE1−/PDPN−), with three children: **Arterial EC** (GJA4, HEY1), **Capillary EC** (CA4, PLVAP) and **Venous EC** (ACKR1).
- **gd T cells:** TRDC alone is also found in NK cells and ILCs. They now also need TRDV1 or TRGV4, and are CD8B−.

**Missing negative markers** (for types that share KIT, ITLN or CPA3)
- Mast cells: ANO1−
- ICC: HDC−
- ILCs: KLRF1−
- Goblet cells: ITLN2−
- Pericytes: PECAM1− and PDGFRA−

**Added cell types**
- **Paneth cells** (ITLN2, ITLN1, SPINK4). The built-in list leaves them out because the panel has no DEFA5/6 or LYZ. ITLN2 is reported as specific to Paneth cells in human small intestine ([Nonnecke et al. 2022](https://figshare.le.ac.uk/articles/journal_contribution/Human_intelectin-2_ITLN2_is_selectively_expressed_by_secretory_Paneth_cells/19383596/1), [HPA](https://www.proteinatlas.org/ENSG00000158764-ITLN2/structure), [Burclaff et al.](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9043569)).
- **Eosinophils** under Myeloid (CLC, CCR3).
- **Follicular dendritic cells** (FDCSP, CLU, FCER2), for Peyer's patches. I found sources for FDCSP and CLU ([celltype.info](https://celltype.info/project/389/dataset/825/label/135112), [JEM 2025](https://rupress.org/jem/article/223/3/e20250471/278568/)) but none for FCER2 (CD23); that one is my addition from standard knowledge.
- **Fibroblast subtypes:** **PDGFRA-hi telocytes** (F3, BMP5, SOX6) and **PDGFRA-lo fibroblasts** (C7, ADH1B or OGN). The telocyte markers rest mostly on mouse studies ([PMC7412576](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7412576)) and on the colon's S2 fibroblasts, so check them against your data.

pDCs are still left out: the panel has none of their markers.

I've sent my proposal to the Refine window for round 1. It has 19 edits grouped by problem, two prior findings and two questions; the server found no problems in the edited list. I didn't change the annotation.

**Edits I recommend:**
- **Paneth cells:** you were right, they are inside Stem cells, as one group of 550 cells at the crypt base. ITLN2 is in 94% of them and in 3% of the other epithelial cells. The old Paneth markers ITLN1 and SPINK4 also mark goblet cells here, which is why Paneth cells got no cells. The edit gives Paneth cells ITLN2, KLK12, SEC11C and AZGP1, and adds KLK12 as a negative marker to Stem cells and Goblet cells.
- **Blood vessels:** only 313 of the 2,633 Arterial EC are arterial (HEY1 in 82%, BMX in 37%). Most of the rest look like capillaries. The 22 cells called Capillary EC look like myeloid cells (CYBB, CD14). New markers for Arterial, Capillary and Venous EC fix this. The capillary markers (CD36, CA4) are the least checked: their share within the would-be capillary group wasn't measured.
- **Weak or unspecific markers replaced** in Cycling TAs, Enterocytes, Goblet cells, Effector/memory CD4 T cells, Naive CD4 T cells, ILCs, PDGFRA-hi telocytes, PDGFRA-lo fibroblasts and Migratory DCs.

**Optional edits (unticked in the window):**
- **gd T cells:** they got no cells, and 57% of the cells called NK cells carry TRDC (a gd T-cell gene). This edit would call these cells gd T cells; I didn't check how many of them also carry CD3E.
- **ACTG2+ DES+ myofibroblasts:** a new type for 417 contractile cells now inside the telocytes. It needs the next edit too: dropping MYH11- from Fibroblasts.
- **Eosinophils:** removing them, because this panel barely detects their genes (CLC in 5 of 2,487 myeloid cells).

**Prior findings:** the Paneth cells hidden in Stem cells (against rule SI-02, likely mislabel) and the myeloid-like cells called Capillary EC.

**Questions for you:**
- Does this section have Peyer's patches or lymphoid follicles? Follicular dendritic cells weren't found; if there are none, the type can go.
- Should cDC2 stay as it is or merge into Dendritic cells? Its marker is weak and it is often confused with Monocytes.

The edits were proposed in my earlier answer, which used [Nonnecke et al. 2022](https://figshare.le.ac.uk/articles/journal_contribution/Human_intelectin-2_ITLN2_is_selectively_expressed_by_secretory_Paneth_cells/19383596/1) and the [Human Protein Atlas](https://www.proteinatlas.org/ENSG00000158764-ITLN2/structure) for ITLN2 as a Paneth cell marker.

You accepted the names, and they now show in the niche legend for both slices of the project. Three of them (N6, N7 and N8) are guesses for the other slice, 167799: 147328 has 12 cells in N6 and none in N7 or N8.

| Niche | Name | Make-up | On the H&E |
|---|---|---|---|
| N1 | **muscularis** | 66% smooth muscle, some PDGFRA-lo fibroblasts, pericytes and glia | the thick muscle at the bottom (rows T–AA), plus the muscle band under the mucosa (rows H–L) |
| N2 | **submucosa** | PDGFRA-lo fibroblasts, venous EC, pericytes, macrophages | the loose tissue with large vessels between the mucosa and the muscle (rows L–T) |
| N3 | **lamina propria** | PDGFRA-hi telocytes, CD4 and CD8 T cells, venous EC; about 26 µm from the epithelium | the cores of the villi and the tissue between the crypts |
| N4 | **villus epithelium** | 84% enterocytes, goblet cells, BEST4+ enterocytes | the villi at the top (rows A–G) |
| N5 | **crypts** | cycling TAs, goblet cells, stem cells | the crypts (rows E–J); the round crypt profiles on the right are in this niche |
| N6 | **goblet-rich crypt epithelium** | 12 cells: goblet, Paneth, stem and cycling cells; its gene programme is the goblet one (ITLN1, RETNLB, REP15) | too few cells in 147328 to place on the H&E |
| N7 | **colonocyte epithelium** | no cells here; programme CD24, SELENBP1, SLC26A2 | — |
| N8 | **colonic surface epithelium** | no cells here; programme SLC26A3, CEACAM5, CEACAM7 | — |

The project is called ileum_colon, and N7 and N8 carry colon-type epithelial genes, so I named them as colon epithelium. Look at them on slice 167799; if they don't fit there, they can be renamed in one call.

I drew the **mucosa** region and you accepted it, so it is now in the annotation (version 3): one piece of 28,674 cells, covering 3.6 mm².

- **How it was drawn:** the outline follows the epithelial cells and the PDGFRA-hi telocytes that sit under the epithelium, with the gaps between villi and crypts filled in. 97% of those cells are inside it.
- **What is inside:** 65% epithelial cells, 14% fibroblasts (mostly lamina propria), 8% T and NK cells, then endothelial, myeloid and mast cells.
- **Against the H&E:** the outline matches the image. The top edge runs along the villus tips and the bottom edge along the crypt bases, against the pink muscle band below. That boundary is around row J on the left and row G on the right.
- **Check one spot:** the dense purple, immune-rich patch at the bottom left (rows J–K, columns 1–6) is mostly outside the outline. If that is mucosa or a lymphoid follicle you want included, extend the region there in the app.

With the region in place, the small-intestine region priors can now apply, for example SI-01 (epithelium only in the mucosa) or SI-09 (plasma cells enriched in the mucosa). I can propose one if you want.

items.title: Enterocytes here are colonocytes: use colon markers
items.text: The list is the small-intestine list. In this sigmoid colon its Enterocytes markers APOB (13%) and MGAM (5%) are hardly detected, while the 3,640 cells carry colonocyte genes: CEACAM7 90%, TMIGD1 89%, AQP8 67% (5-7% of the other epithelial cells). Rename Enterocytes to Colonocytes with CEACAM7+ AQP8+ TMIGD1+ (or start from the built-in colon list) so the type and the colon priors (COL-03) match.

action.request: Propose the marker-list edit: Enterocytes renamed Colonocytes with CEACAM7+ AQP8+ TMIGD1+ BEST4- OTOP2-, checked with check_marker_list.

items.title: BEST4+ enterocytes too many (806, only ~106 real)
items.text: Only sub-cluster /1 (106 cells, spatial clustering 2.79) is BEST4+ (BEST4 90%, OTOP2 84%, SPIB 81%, CA4 79%; 10-18% in the rest of the type). The other ~700 cells lack BEST4 (27% overall) and look like CA1+ colonocytes. Require BEST4 together with OTOP2 or CA4 so the type keeps only real BEST4+ cells (COL-03 notes these cells are lost in IBD, so their number matters).

action.request: Propose BEST4+ enterocytes: BEST4+ OTOP2+ CA4+ SPIB+ CCL20-, with the shares above.

items.title: Eosinophils are LYVE1+ macrophages
items.text: The 118 Eosinophils have no eosinophil transcripts (CLC 0%, CCR3 2%); 70 of them are LYVE1+ (70% vs 15%) and the rest ITGAX+ ACTG2+, i.e. macrophages (confusion with Macrophages 0.30). The panel cannot detect eosinophils: remove the type so these cells return to Macrophages.

action.request: Propose removing Eosinophils from the marker list.

items.title: cDC2 cells are cDC1
items.text: The 100 cells called cDC2 have CLEC9A in 85%, IRF8 in 93 of 99 DCs and CLEC10A in 2%: they are cDC1, which got no cells. Relabel them cDC1 (e.g. drop the CLEC10A- negative from cDC1 or merge cDC2 into Dendritic cells for this sample).

action.request: Propose a marker-list edit so these CLEC9A+ IRF8+ cells become cDC1.

items.title: 764 Unassigned cells are subepithelial telocytes
items.text: The Unassigned cells sit at the epithelium (depth 0) and carry the PDGFRA-hi telocyte programme: POSTN 78%, EDNRB 60%, F3 54%, BMP5 31% (10-20% elsewhere). Telocyte marker BMP5 is weak (17%); add EDNRB or POSTN to PDGFRA-hi telocytes (e.g. F3|BMP5+ EDNRB|POSTN+) so they are typed.

action.request: Propose PDGFRA-hi telocytes markers F3|BMP5+ EDNRB|POSTN+ and check that the Unassigned cells move there.

items.title: Smooth muscle in the lamina propria: do not exclude it from the mucosa
items.text: The 7 review areas are all vessel walls or muscularis mucosae; in A3 spindle muscle fibres rise between crypts, which COL-10 lists as an exception in diverticular disease (this sample: diverticulitis). Keep COL-10 as an enrich rule only; do not add a smooth-muscle exclusion from the mucosa.

items.title: Interferon-high epithelial patch
items.text: Enterocytes sub-cluster /7 (268 cells) forms one tight patch (spatial clustering 10.7) with IFIT1 99%, RSAD2 95%, DDX58 95% and LAMP3 36%: an interferon response, likely inflamed mucosa near the diverticulitis. It is real biology, not a mislabel; worth a region or a look on the H&E.

items.title: Registration and spill-over fine
items.text: Registration: offset 0 um, max 5.2 um at the corners, no correction needed. Epithelial-marker spill-over falls with distance (59% <10 um, 10% >60 um), the usual segmentation pattern; no tile hotspots of low transcripts.

c16_biology.text: Is there anything biologically interesting in these two sections that I should look at?

Three things look worth your time, one in the colon and two in the ileum. Both sections come from a diverticulitis patient (labelled non-IBD controls). All of this comes from the annotations I reviewed; none of it is confirmed beyond what I note.

**Sigmoid colon (167799)**

1. **A patch of interferon-activated epithelium.** 268 absorptive cells form a single tight cluster, about ten times more clumped than chance. Nearly all of them carry interferon-response genes (IFIT1 99%, RSAD2 95%, DDX58 95%, IFIH1 91%), and a third carry LAMP3. This most likely marks an inflamed focus near the diverticulitis. I haven't found it on the H&E, so I can't yet rule out a technical artefact. Looking at it there, and at the immune cells around it, is the first thing I'd do.
2. **Muscle fibres rising between the crypts.** At tile S7, spindle-shaped smooth muscle runs up from the muscularis mucosae between the crypt bases. That is a known feature of diverticular disease, and the H&E supports it.

**Terminal ileum (147328)**

3. **An organized lymphoid area.** B cells, naive CD4 T cells and CCR7+ LAMP3+ migratory DCs cluster together, deep under the epithelium. That looks like a lymphoid follicle or Peyer's patch: on the H&E it is probably the dense purple area at rows J–K, columns 1–6, just below the mucosa outline we drew. Two things argue against a full patch: no follicular dendritic cells or M cells were found, and the panel's markers for them are weak. Looking at the H&E there would tell you whether it is an isolated follicle or a patch, and whether its epithelium is the specialized kind that covers patches.

**Smaller points:**
- **Ileum:** 1,452 mast cells (2.6% of cells), about a fifth of them right against the epithelium. That is plausible for the ileum, but on the high side.
- **Ileum:** a few neutrophils cluster next to submucosal veins, as if leaving the vessels. There are only 116, so it is weak evidence of active inflammation.
- **Colon:** glia make up 4.5% of cells (1,861), against 1.6% in the ileum. This could be biology or simply because the colon section holds more muscle and plexus; I haven't checked which.

I can show you the interferon patch on the H&E with its neighbouring cell types, or outline the lymphoid area in the ileum as a region.
